The Master of Art in User Experience/User Interface (UX/UI) Design is a stackable master's that combines the four-course Graduate Certificate in User Experience Design, developed by WRT, and the four-course Graduate Certificate in User Interface Design, created by ART, augmented by two additional courses.
The thirty-credit program will prepare students for meaningful careers in the burgeoning fields of UX/UI.
This online accelerated dual-focus curriculum offers students— including those with full-time jobs—a flexible path to gaining proficiency with the tools and approaches of the closely related fields of UX and UI research and design, opening a broad range of lucrative career opportunities.
Students emerge from this program as versatile professionals capable of addressing complex design challenges.
Their skills span from the intricate details of UI elements to the strategic considerations of holistic user experiences.
Armed with the knowledge of both UX and UI, graduates become adept at designing solutions that merge aesthetics, functionality, and human-centered values.
The program is unique in its emphasis on the ethical implications of research and design processes and products.

The UX Certificate nurtures an understanding of user behavior, needs, and expectations through rigorous research, ensuring accessibility and accessible design.
UX courses guide students in creating designs that prioritize inclusivity, social justice, sustainability, and user well-being.
They also offer students cutting-edge approaches to UX writing and interaction design.
The UI Design Certificate provides students with the crucial knowledge, and the technical and practical skills, to become proficient UI designers.
Students will create interface projects integrating branding, animation, patternmaking, and front-end visualizations to depict intuitive user experiences, enabling them to craft interactions that leave a lasting impact.
Students in the Master's Program are able to take UI Visual Principles for Non-designers, which helps them develop a unique approach to the design process with the user interface experience in mind (advanced designers may also select an approved elective from other URIO offerings).
The two certificates then culminate in WRT/ART 509: UX/UI Portfolio.

In this cross-listed course (WRT and ART), students integrate and apply the knowledge and skills they have gained in their UX and UI Design Certificate courses to create compelling, effective, polished portfolios that demonstrate their expertise to potential employers and clients.
Additionally, the course will focus on professionalization for careers in UX, UI, and related design fields.
Graduates of this program will have the capability to examine how individuals navigate real-life scenarios, empowering them to enhance experiences by creating new design-centered connections.
They will possess the abilities to recognize limitations and openings for enhancing interactions between objects, systems—whether virtual or physical—as well as the people who interact with them.
In an ever-evolving technological landscape, the Master of Arts in UX/UI Design equips students to stand at the forefront of innovation, transcending traditional boundaries between the two fields.

ART 505: UI Design: Styling and Prototyping introduces students to the theory and practice of user interface design, focusing on visual communication tools and skills to facilitate prototyping.

ART 506: UI Motion Design introduces motion design in user experience within a framework of the three foundational principles of communication, orientation, and correlation.
Students will learn how motion design can complement visual affordances to provide users with more meaningful experiences and interactions.
It explores motion design as a sequence of movements that affects the user’s perception of any interface a user interacts with.

ART 507: UI Icon Design introduces and develops the skills needed to conceptualize and design icons for user interfaces.
The context, design and application of UI icons will be critiqued based on the effectiveness and appropriateness of the design language.
